correctness.rationale: For b<d the predator decays and the positive ODE stays global. The F-curve has two simple positive roots, the lower hyperbolic saddle has eigenvalues lambda_u<0<lambda_z and its stable graph has slope kappa=z_-/(lambda_u-lambda_z). A two-chart uniform ratio bound treats all z0=v0/u0, including arbitrarily large ratios, and local invariant strips establish exact rescue/extinction partition for the small square. Integrating v=u s(u) with the appropriate top-boundary clipping proves the two formulas with O(epsilon^2) error. Independent root calculations and opposite-side trajectories were checked; finite experiments do not prove the theorem.

value.rationale: The quantity is the natural initial-condition area share of deterministic extinction when both populations are small. The explicit positive correction captures how ecological extinction risk shifts as initial sampling density changes, while the z_-=1 change in square clipping is a real, natural boundary phenomenon. Uniform treatment of unbounded predator/prey ratios is essential and not automatic from a local saddle expansion.
